To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
working memory biasing of perceptual selection is independent of conscious awareness.
working memory biasing of the perceptual system can operate in the context of continuous flash suppression and can operate in the complete absence of awareness.
visual working memory can influence visual perception even when the memory contents are nonconscious.
In summary, our research is concerned with
visual perception and working memory.
the relationship between conscious and unconscious processes in the visual domain.
the question of what is the role of working memory in visual perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
working memory biasing of perception can occur without awareness, and that the biasing is independent of the awareness of both the cue in working memory and the cue in the visual scene.
working memory biasing of perceptual selection is not contingent on conscious awareness.
working memory biases perceptual selection in favor of stimuli that match the contents of memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biasing effect of working memory on visual perception is independent of conscious awareness.
the contents of working memory can bias perceptual selection processes even in the absence of awareness of both the cue and the target.
visual working memory bias of visual processing can operate in the presence or absence of conscious awareness, depending on the task demands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contents of working memory can bias perceptual processing even in the absence of visual consciousness.
the biasing of perceptual selection by working memory can be dissociated from conscious perception.

working memory is not only a repository for information that is consciously available but also a source of top-down biasing of visual processing that operates even for information that is rendered invisible.
